title: Flat Mittag-Leffler criterion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module] if and only if the following property holds: for every $R$-module $F$ isomorphic to $R^n$ for some finite integer $n\geq0$ and every $x\in F\otimes_R M$, the set of submodules $G\subseteq F$ for which $x$ belongs to the image of $G\otimes_R M\to F\otimes_R M$ has a least element under inclusion. The displayed map is induced by $G\hookrightarrow F$ and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Assume first that $M$ is Mittag-Leffler. Since $M$ is flat, the auxiliary least-support lemma [lem-trf-flat-ml-minimal-support] applies to the finite free module $F$ and the element $x$. It gives a smallest submodule $F_0\subseteq F$ whose tensor image contains $x$, exactly the property required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 059S proof, implication (1) to (2), invoking Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains).

proof.text: Conversely, assume the least-submodule property for every finite free $F$. Given a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] at $A$, $B$ and $C$, including the zero endpoints. Thus $-\otimes_R M$ preserves short exact sequences, using the given flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. By [lem-kun-lazard-flat-module], $M$ has a presentation by a small nonempty directed poset $I$, finite free modules $(M_i,f_{ij})$, and compatible colimit maps $f_i:M_i\to M$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 059S proof, paragraph beginning "By Theorem theorem-lazard"; Tag 00HD for flat tensor exactness.

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and put $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,R)$. By [lem-trf-finite-free-map-coefficient-support], $H$ is finite free and the natural isomorphisms $\Phi_N$ give tensors $x_i=\Phi_{M_i}^{-1}(1_{M_i})$, $x_j=\Phi_{M_j}^{-1}(f_{ij})$, and $x=\Phi_M^{-1}(f_i)$. Naturality gives $x_j=(1_H\otimes f_{ij})x_i$ and $x=(1_H\otimes f_i)x_i$. For each $j\ge i$, the same lemma says that $Q_j=\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,R)\to H)$ is the least support of $x_j$; here precomposition sends $\lambda$ to $\lambda\circ f_{ij}$. For $k\ge j\ge i$, compatibility $f_{ik}=f_{jk}f_{ij}$ and naturality also give $x_k=(1_H\otimes f_{jk})x_j$.

Apply the assumed least-submodule property to the finite free module $H$ and $x$, obtaining its least support $Q$. Apply [lem-trf-directed-tensor-least-support-stabilization] to $(M_j,f_{jk})$, $H$, $i$, $x_i$, and the least supports $Q_j$ from Step 3. It gives $Q\subseteq Q_j$ for all $j\ge i$ and an index $j_0\ge i$ with $Q_k=Q_{j_0}=Q$ for every $k\ge j_0$. Thus the images of the precomposition maps into $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,R)$ stabilize for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), commutative square and final stabilization paragraph.

proof.text: The small nonempty directed finite-free presentation of Step 2, the original flatness of $M$, and stabilization from Step 4 satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-trf-flat-ml-dual-criterion]. It follows that $M$ is Mittag-Leffler. Together with Step 1 this proves the equivalence.

reviewed_lean.note: Read the node, the three statement dependencies, Stacks 059M/0AS6/059S, Module.IsMittagLeffler (universes u v w t) and the delivered module and report (both report sections present). The clauses match the node, but two free universes made the statement false at some instantiations (H3). (1) IsMittagLeffler's index universe was auto-bound and free: below R's universe the predicate is weaker, and the forward direction fails (the fraction field of a valuation domain whose value group has cofinality at least |Type 0| passes it with no least support for 1). Pinned to IsMittagLeffler.{u, v, max u s, t}. (2) F : Type w with w free: below R's universe only n = 0 occurs, so the reverse direction would make every flat module ML. Pinned to F : Type (max u w). No generality is lost (ULift transfers to smaller universes; the finite-free condition is invariant under transport). The docstring now gives the node's six proof steps.
